facts.text: A lottery ticket worth €1 million (about US$1.15 million) was recovered from waste on a garbage truck in Bitonto, Italy.
Roberto Nicola Toscano is an administrator at the SANB waste management company, based in Italy's Puglia region.
Toscano said the recovered ticket was still intact after workers searched through the trash on the truck.
The woman played the lottery on Saturday and checked her ticket at a local shop the following Sunday, after the drawing.
The shop's machine displayed the message "non-payable" when the ticket was checked.
A "non-payable" message indicates the prize is too large for a small retailer to pay out, as smaller Italian retailers can only redeem small lottery wins.
A family member recognized the winning combination and told the woman she had won, after she had already thrown the ticket away and returned home.
By the time the woman returned to the shop, the bin containing the ticket had already been emptied by a garbage truck.
Toscano said the woman always played the same numbers because they were connected to a loved one.
According to Corriere Della Sera, the winning number combination was 2, 4, 8, 10 and 51.
The woman asked waste collection workers to help retrieve the discarded ticket.
Toscano said SANB reconstructed the route of the ticket, identified the truck involved and stopped it.
Toscano said the truck was taken to a specially equipped site because searching the waste carried a risk from potentially hazardous material.
Toscano told Corriere Della Sera that workers spent one day searching before locating the ticket.
Toscano told AFP that the woman promised to pay all additional costs of the search, which SANB, as a public entity, would otherwise have charged to taxpayers.
The winner's identity has not been made public.

topics.title: Migrants rescued after Channel boat fire

articles.title: Over 170 migrants rescued after Channel boat catches fire; UK says 'all will be returned' to France
More than 170 migrants rescued after boat catches fire in Channel

facts.text: A small boat attempting to cross the English Channel from France to the UK caught fire in its engine on Tuesday morning.
The French maritime prefecture of the Channel and North Sea said 173 people were rescued and brought ashore at Boulogne-sur-Mer in France.
Eleven migrants sustained minor injuries and no deaths were reported.
French officials said the boat left northern France on Monday night.
The French maritime prefecture said five people on board were rescued during the overnight journey while the other passengers refused assistance offered by French patrol boats.
Rescue vessels from France and the UK attended the scene, including the RNLI Eastbourne lifeboat and UK Border Force vessels.
The operation involved firefighters, police officers, interpreters and medical teams.
French prosecutors opened an investigation into the incident and an Egyptian national was taken into police custody in connection with the case.
The UK government said the Border Security Command was alerted after the migrant small boat got into distress in French waters.
Border Security Minister Anna Turley said the incident showed the dangers of illegal crossings and the gangs behind them.
Shadow home secretary Chris Philp criticised French police for not preventing migrant boats from leaving the French coast.
Home Office figures show total crossings so far this year are lower than at the same point last year.
Britain and France signed a three-year agreement worth £662m on border enforcement aimed at stopping illegal crossings of the Channel, including beach patrols, drones and helicopters.
French authorities said the vessel's structural integrity deteriorated rapidly after the engine fire.
The French maritime prefecture initially reported 157 migrants were rescued and later revised the figure to 173.
UK Border Force vessels involved were BSC Contender and BSC Courageous.
The French maritime prefecture said the operation involved 40 firefighters, 13 police officers and seven interpreters.
Two French boats rescued 105 migrants and British boats rescued 63, in addition to the five rescued initially.
The UK government said those on board were returned to France.
Reform UK proposed deploying the Royal Navy to deter migrant boats under a plan called "Operation Fortress".
Reform UK leader Nigel Farage wrote on X that the crossings must be stopped and that his party's plan will save lives.
UK authorities said 752 migrants arrived in Britain in small boats last Wednesday, the highest daily total recorded in 2026.
Home Office figures show crossings so far this year are about 43% lower than at the same point last year.
The UK-France deal was agreed in April.

topics.title: Toddler dies with head trapped in toy kitchen in Florida

articles.title: 3-year-old girl dies after getting head stuck in kitchen playset: Police
Florida 3-year-old dies after tragic incident involving common play toy at babysitter's house

facts.text: A 3-year-old girl in Boynton Beach, Florida, died after her head became stuck in a toy kitchen playset, according to police.
The child died on July 27, according to police.
The incident occurred while the toddler and her sibling were at a babysitter's house.
Police said the babysitter had left the residence and the children were in the care of the babysitter's spouse.
Police said the spouse remained upstairs while the children played downstairs, periodically checking on them and giving them snacks.
Police said the spouse went downstairs and found the 3-year-old with her head stuck in the kitchen playset.
Police said the child was not breathing/unresponsive when found.
Police said the spouse removed the child from the playset and performed life-saving measures until first responders arrived shortly after 11 a.m.
The toddler was transported by Boynton Beach Fire Rescue to a local hospital in critical condition, where she remained until her death.
Police said the child's sibling told investigators that toys had fallen inside the play kitchen and the child became stuck while trying to retrieve them.
The investigation is ongoing and no criminal charges have been filed.
Authorities have not released the toddler's cause and manner of death.
The girl was identified by relatives as Briella.
Officers responded to the Meadows of Boynton Beach community shortly after 11 a.m. on July 23 following a report of a child not breathing.
Authorities have not released the toddler's name.
A police spokesperson said the wooden kitchen playset had been purchased on Facebook Marketplace a few years earlier and that its make and model were not known at the time.
A GoFundMe fundraiser created after the girl's death stated that donations will go toward funeral and memorial expenses.
Fox News Digital said it contacted the Palm Beach County Medical Examiner's Office about the cause and manner of death and did not immediately receive a response.

articles.title: White House revokes visa of Brazil's ambassador to US: reports
U.S. Revokes Brazilian Ambassador’s Visa Amid Diplomatic Standoff

facts.text: The Trump administration revoked the visa of Brazil's ambassador to the United States.
Brazil's ambassador to the United States is Maria Luiza Ribeiro Viotti.
The visa revocation followed Brazil's denial of visas to two American diplomats who sought to travel to Brazil before upcoming elections.
A State Department official told the Associated Press on condition of anonymity that Viotti is not being expelled from the United States despite the visa revocation.
A State Department official told Reuters that the visa would be restored if Brazil grants agreement to the US ambassadorial nominee.

Brazil announced last month that it denied visas to officials from the US State Department's Bureau of Democracy, Human Rights and Labor, saying their planned visit was intended to undermine Brazil's electoral system before the October elections.

The State Department said the two officials had planned to visit Brasilia in late July to meet government officials, religious leaders and others regarding election integrity, religious freedom and freedom of expression.
Brazil withheld formal approval of Daniel Perez, a Florida state representative, as US ambassador for several weeks.
Donald Trump nominated Daniel Perez as ambassador to Brazil on June 1.
Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva is the president of Brazil.
Jair Bolsonaro is serving a 27-year sentence under house arrest for plotting a coup after losing the 2022 election to Lula.
Flavio Bolsonaro is a right-wing presidential candidate in Brazil's October vote.
Brazil is scheduled to hold an election in October.
The visa revocation occurred amid a diplomatic standoff or clash between the United States and Brazil involving the Trump administration.

articles.title: US stock market hits record highs as AI profits pile and oil prices ease
S&P 500 Hits Record High as Stock Market Worries About Iran and AI Ease

facts.text: The S&P 500 rose 1.8%, closing at 7,736.52 after gaining 136.02 points on Tuesday.
The S&P 500 moved above its previous high, which had been reached at the start of June.
The rise in the S&P 500 followed a recent decline in technology stocks.
Stock market concerns about Iran and artificial intelligence had eased.
The Dow Jones industrial average rose 907.47 points, or 1.7%, to 54,085.88.
The Nasdaq composite gained 671.10 points, or 2.6%, to 26,584.99.
Palantir Technologies shares rose 29.5% after the company reported quarterly results.
Palantir CEO Alex Karp said the company's overall revenue rose 93% in the quarter and described the quarter as "otherworldly".
Palantir raised its revenue forecast for the full year of 2026.
Caterpillar shares rose 5.6% after the company reported profit and revenue above analysts' expectations.
Caterpillar recorded more than $20bn in sales and revenue in a quarter for the first time.
Caterpillar CEO Joe Creed said the company was seeing strong order rates and a growing backlog across its main businesses.
According to FactSet, S&P 500 companies were on track to report nearly 50% growth in earnings per share for the spring quarter compared with a year earlier.
Brent crude fell 5.3% to $79.36 per barrel.
The yield on the 10-year treasury fell to 4.62%, from 4.70% on Monday and 4.75% at the end of the prior week.
Nvidia shares rose 2.6%, Broadcom shares rose 6.6% and Micron Technology shares rose 7.6%.
Chipotle Mexican Grill shares fell 9.7% after the chain removed jalapeños from some restaurants following a salmonella outbreak.
Chipotle said Minnesota health officials have no ongoing concerns with the company.
